key_insight: Topology-guided flow control combines vortex-aware target selection with reduced-order predictive control to reduce mean drag while preserving main vortices.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a computationally streamlined strategy for active aerodynamic control around an oscillating wing.
method: Detect and characterize vortices using persistence diagrams of absolute vorticity.
Compute a target retaining useful vortices offline via gradient descent in a DMDc reduced space.
Track the target with receding-horizon MPC using a small-dimensional convex quadratic program.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests of flow around an oscillating aircraft wing at seven vibration frequencies yielded mean drag-coefficient reductions while preserving main vortices.
watch_item: Evidence is numerical; experimental robustness and performance beyond the tested vibration frequencies remain unestablished.
paper_title: Active flow control based on topological data analysis and a DMDc reduced-order model for drag reduction
